chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was absent in another town, and he witnessed her divorce with two men. Then he returned to her before the expiration of the waiting period, but did not witness the return. Then he arrived at her after the expiration of the waiting period, and she had married another man. So he sent to her saying: 'I had returned to you before the expiration of the waiting period, but I did not witness it.' He said: 'He has no claim over her because he acknowledged the divorce and claimed the return without evidence, and he has no claim over her. And thus it is proper for the one who divorces to witness, and for the one who returns to witness the return, just as he witnessed the divorce. If he reached her before she married, he would be suitor among the suitors.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal requirement for witnessing a husband's return to his wife during the Islamic waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq establishes the principle that a man's unilateral claim of remarriage (raj'a) without witnesses is insufficient to prevent the wife from entering a new marriage, thereby protecting her status. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on procedural justice and evidentiary requirements in family law, ensuring that the husband's right to reclaim his wife is not asserted arbitrarily after she has become legally available to others.
